## Which tour includes Bouza Winery?

[Bouza Winery](/uruguay/place/bouza-winery/) is located near Montevideo. It features in the [“Best of Uruguay: Five-Star Tour”](/uruguay/tour/best-of-uruguay-five-star-tour/). This 6-day journey combines wine experiences with the capital's architecture, the coast and time in [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/).

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Bouza occupies one of the winery days, so choose the itinerary based on the whole journey: accommodation, transfers, excursions and dining stops, not merely the name of one winery.

## Day at Bouza Winery: what's included

Bouza is visited on day 3, while travelers are still staying in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). After breakfast, the itinerary includes a trip to the vineyards and winery. A **3-course lunch** follows, with a wine selected for each course to explore pairings of local food and wine.

The lunch is a substantial part of the experience. During the visit, guests discover the estate and then compare how the wines complement different dishes. Afterward, they return to their city hotel at the agreed time.

The winery visit, 3-course lunch and paired wines are listed among the tour's included services. The exact length of the visit and the specific tasting selection are not stated, so these details should be agreed for the selected departure.

## Why the itinerary also includes Garzón Winery

The second winery stop belongs to another stage. After 3 nights in Montevideo, travelers transfer to Punta del Este, then visit [Garzón Winery](/uruguay/place/garzon-winery/) on day 5. The Reserva experience includes a tour, tasting and seasonal **4-course lunch with paired wines**.

Bouza is convenient for exploring wine production while based in the capital. Garzón adds another experience from Punta del Este, after the move to the Atlantic coast. These two visits allow travelers to compare estates and dining formats without turning the entire 6-day journey into an uninterrupted wine tour.

For travelers primarily interested in wineries and tastings, see [food and wine tours in Uruguay](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/uruguay/). The separate [Bouza page](/uruguay/place/bouza-winery/) describes the winery itself.

## What happens between the two tastings?

The 6-day itinerary integrates the wineries into stays in two cities.

**Montevideo, first 3 nights.** After arrival, guests check into Hyatt Centric Montevideo. The next day brings a private tour of the capital: Independence Square, Solís Theatre, Palacio Salvo, the historic market and the coastal Rambla. Day 3 includes Bouza and its wine-pairing lunch.

**Punta del Este, next 2 nights.** Day 4 involves a private transfer and a stay at The Grand Punta del Este. A private tour takes in the peninsula, harbor, La Mano sculpture and Casapueblo, where a sunset visit is planned. Garzón Winery is scheduled for the following day. Day 6 includes a transfer to Montevideo airport or port.

The program specifies River View rooms at Hyatt Centric Montevideo and Ocean View Junior rooms at The Grand Punta del Este, private excursions conducted in English and the listed private transfers. If the organizer replaces a hotel, the agreed accommodation category is maintained. Extra excursions are not included in the listed services.

## Who will enjoy a journey featuring Bouza?

The itinerary is especially suitable for travelers who want to discover Uruguayan wine while also leaving time for cities, the ocean and food. Bouza takes up one day; the other main components are [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/).

If you only want a brief winery visit without traveling to the coast, the current catalog alone does not confirm a separate one- or two-day product. Discuss such a request individually, distinguishing a possible tailored itinerary from the published ready-made tour.

Before choosing, compare meals, guiding language, accommodation and transfer convenience. For trips across the country, use our [Uruguay tour catalog](/uruguay/tour/). Ada Tours can help align the winery visits with the rest of the journey and the group's interests.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Bouza

### Which day includes the Bouza visit?

The confirmed 6-day itinerary visits the winery on day 3, during the 3-night stay in Montevideo.

### Are the tasting and lunch included in the price?

The included-services list specifies a visit to Bouza and a 3-course lunch with paired wines. Check the exact wine selection for your visit.

### How does Bouza differ from Garzón on this tour?

Both wineries belong to the same journey but appear at different stages. Bouza is visited from Montevideo, while Garzón is visited during the stay in Punta del Este. Bouza includes a 3-course lunch, while Garzón includes the Reserva tour and a seasonal 4-course lunch.

## Canelones: Uruguay's wine-producing heartland

Canelones is a region of [Uruguay](/uruguay/) with a high concentration of vineyards and wineries. It is near the capital area, so a wine excursion can be added to a trip from [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) or to a journey linking cultural attractions with the Atlantic coast.

Local estates are known for family traditions and wines made from **Tannat** grapes. According to the Canelones regional tourism authority, more than 60% of Uruguay's wineries are located here. The wine region nevertheless spans several towns and rural areas, so choose a specific estate, tour time and tasting program in advance.

## Why is Canelones associated with Tannat?

Tannat is a red grape variety brought from Europe that has become one of Uruguay's signature grapes. Winemakers in the region work with its structure and rich flavor, producing different styles, from young, fruit-forward wines to aged versions with more pronounced tannins.

A tasting helps compare not only grape varieties but also production methods. Ripeness, oak barrels, aging and winemakers' decisions all influence the result. Visiting several wineries can therefore reveal more about the region than buying one bottle with a familiar label.

Family continuity plays a major role. The Canelones tourism portal highlights estates where knowledge passes through generations and visitors can meet the winemakers and owners themselves.

## What happens on a winery tour?

A typical visit to an operating winery may include a walk through the vineyards, an explanation of growing the vines, a tour of production facilities and a tasting. However, which activities are included depends on the chosen estate and season.

Useful questions to ask in advance include:

- Does the visit cover the vineyards and production rooms, or only the tasting room?
- How many wines are included, and can you compare Tannat from different years?
- Is guiding available in your preferred language, and is advance booking required?
- Can you book a lunch or wine pairing with regional food?

Regional cuisine complements local wine. Uruguay's meat dishes allow guests to explore how different red wines pair with food. But a tasting and a full lunch are separate services; no particular menu should be promised without confirmation from the winery.

## Choosing a winery

Canelones has estates with different histories, locations and visitor formats. The official tourism catalog includes Antigua Bodega Stagnari and other producers, but being listed does not confirm availability for your chosen date.

| Your priority | Visit format |
|---|---|
| Learn about Tannat | Taste several wines |
| Understand production | Tour the facilities |
| Enjoy the countryside | Walk among the vines |
| Relax over food | Wine-pairing lunch |

For a first introduction, one well-planned visit with a meaningful explanation and enough tasting time can be sufficient. A tightly packed sequence of stops reduces the value of each encounter.

Wineries are spread across different parts of the department, and the distance between two addresses can be substantial. Canelones should not be treated as one compact, walkable wine village.

## Vineyard seasons and practical preparation

The vine-growing year in the Southern Hemisphere differs from Europe's. Landscapes change as vines grow and grapes ripen, while harvest timing depends on weather and grape variety. To see the grape harvest or processing, arrange it with a particular estate: the date is not identical every year.

Comfortable shoes are useful on vineyard paths. For tastings, arrange a driver or another means of return transport in advance, avoiding driving after consuming alcohol.

Canelones also has rural landscapes, small towns and other cultural attractions. Nevertheless, keep the purpose of a wine-focused trip in mind: allow time for the vineyard, production and conversation with a winemaker.

## Canelones in Ada Tours programs

Our [16-day tour through Uruguay and Paraguay](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) includes a separate day in Canelones with a Tannat tasting and an onward journey to [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/). The combination introduces wine culture before moving on to coastal towns.

Other Uruguay programs include [Spinoglio Winery](/uruguay/place/spinoglio-winery/) and separate tasting stops. One winery's terms cannot automatically be applied to another. If wine is a particular interest, explore more [food and wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Frequently asked questions about Canelones

### Is Canelones a town or a wine region?

There is a town called Canelones as well as a department of the same name. This page covers **the wine region**, encompassing several towns and estates.

### What is the main wine here?

Uruguay's best-known grape variety is Tannat. Many wineries also produce wines from other grapes, so tastings can be varied.

### Can you visit a winery without booking?

Do not rely on this. Tastings, production tours and lunches may require separate reservations and have restrictions on times or guest numbers.

### Do you need a full day?

One winery visit may be enough for a first introduction. For two wineries or a lunch, allow a substantial part of the day, including transfers.

## Tours through Canelones: wineries, Tannat and travel across Uruguay

Canelones lies in Uruguay's wine region near Montevideo. Visitors come for wineries, vineyards, local cuisine and Tannat wine. To choose a trip, it is more useful to find out **how much time is spent at a winery and what comes next** than to look for the word “wine” in a tour title.

In the Ada Tours catalog, the [16-day Uruguay and Paraguay tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) passes through [Canelones](/uruguay/place/canelones/). It combines Uruguay's coastal cities, inland Paraguay and Iguazu Falls. Canelones occupies one full excursion day, not the entire holiday.

## What the winery day includes

On day 3, travelers head to Canelones after exploring Montevideo and the historic district of Colonia del Sacramento. The program includes **a boutique winery visit, wine tasting and lunch among the vineyards**. In the afternoon, the itinerary continues to [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) on the Atlantic coast.

Uruguay is known for red wines made from Tannat grapes. This variety is especially prominent in Canelones, often producing wine with a rich color and noticeable tannins. During a winery visit, ask about vine cultivation, production and pairing wine with local food. The specific wine list and name of the estate are not fixed in the current description, so a visit to any particular bodega should not be promised.

**The winery day is part of the main itinerary.** Unlike an independent tasting, it continues to the ocean after lunch. Spending two or three full days visiting several wineries would require another program.

## How Canelones fits into the 16-day route

The first stage takes place in Uruguay. The tour begins in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), then visits Colonia del Sacramento, Canelones and Punta del Este. After the coastal stay, travelers move into Paraguay: Asunción, the Chaco region, Laguna Capitán, local communities and Guairá landscapes.

The final days focus on Iguazu Falls. The itinerary visits both the Brazilian and Argentine sides. Thus **Canelones is one gastronomic stop on a multi-country journey**, where winery experiences are followed by history, nature outings and waterfalls.

| Route segment | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Montevideo and Colonia | Cities, history and old neighborhoods |
| Canelones | Winery, Tannat, tasting and lunch |
| Punta del Este | Atlantic coast and relaxation |
| Paraguay and Iguazu | Inland regions, nature and waterfalls |

Use the actual program to guide your choice. The journey lasts 16 days, but Canelones is visited on a single day. Check the complete sequence of transfers, excursion stops and included services on the [tour page](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/).

## Who will enjoy this journey?

This route suits travelers who want to taste Uruguayan wine in the country where it is produced and then continue exploring South America. The winery day introduces a local estate and flavors without requiring an entire holiday devoted to wine.

If your main aim is to compare many wineries, meet several oenologists and dedicate several days to tastings, consider a more extensive custom wine itinerary. Departure times, capacity of each estate, tasting selection and lunches all matter and are agreed for the particular journey.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. For thematic comparisons, see [Food and Wine](/interests/food-and-wine/); to learn more about the region, visit [Canelones](/uruguay/place/canelones/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Canelones

### Does the tour include a Tannat tasting?

The 16-day program includes a boutique winery visit, wine tasting and lunch. Tannat is characteristic of the region. The exact tasting selection is arranged with the chosen estate.

### Is Canelones a separate tour for the entire holiday?

No. On our itinerary, the Canelones visit takes one excursion day within a journey across several South American countries.

### Do you return to Montevideo after the winery?

No. On this tour, after lunch in Canelones, the route continues to Punta del Este. Returning to the capital at the end of the day 3 winery visit is not scheduled.

### Can wine be the main focus of the trip?

Yes, but visiting several estates and enjoying extended tastings would require a separate itinerary with extra time. This does not automatically change the current 16-day tour.

## Colonia del Sacramento: an old town on the Río de la Plata

[Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) stands on the northern shore of the Río de la Plata estuary, opposite the Argentine side. It is one of [Uruguay's](/uruguay/) best-known historic towns, where low houses, stone walls and cobbled lanes retain traces of the Portuguese and Spanish past.

The main attraction is exploring the historic quarter on foot. It covers a relatively small area but offers fascinating details: old doors, tiled roofs, arches and unexpected views across the broad water. Take your time and allow for side streets, museums and the waterfront.

## Why is Colonia del Sacramento UNESCO-listed?

The town was founded **by the Portuguese in 1680**. It had strategic importance because it allowed control over part of navigation on the Río de la Plata. Portugal and Spain contested possession of the settlement. Periods of siege, destruction and reconstruction left traces in the urban landscape.

The **Historic Quarter** of Colonia del Sacramento was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in **1995**. This status applies to a defined historic area, not automatically to every modern district of the town.

UNESCO particularly emphasizes the quarter's layout. Unlike many Spanish colonial cities with regular rectangular street grids, old Colonia developed more freely, reflecting the land and defensive requirements. The street pattern is as important to understanding the site's heritage as the buildings themselves.

## What to see in the historic center

### Calle de los Suspiros and cobbled lanes

**Calle de los Suspiros**, or Street of Sighs, is known for its old stone paving and low facades. It is one of the best places to appreciate the historical structure of the town. Notice how the street fits into neighboring blocks rather than limiting the walk to one compulsory facade photograph.

### Old gates, walls and squares

Surviving defensive structures recall the days when the town was a fortress and a contested trading post. You can walk from the gates toward the squares, then down to the shore. Small museums help connect the surviving buildings to the histories of Portugal, Spain and independent Uruguay.

### Lighthouse and views over the Río de la Plata

The town lighthouse is a prominent landmark in the old center. From nearby streets, visitors can see the estuary, boats and low shoreline. If access to the viewing platform is available, check its opening hours and conditions separately. Beautiful panoramas can also be enjoyed from the waterfront.

## Colonia beyond the postcard

Colonia is often appreciated as a picturesque backdrop, but its history is more complex. Portuguese, Spanish and later Uruguayan architectural choices coexist in the same urban fabric. Look at masonry techniques, roof shapes, wooden shutters and the scale of houses; these details reveal the town's layered past.

Cafes and restaurants make it convenient to alternate walking with breaks. Museums and smaller heritage sites may have different opening schedules, especially outside the busy season. If a particular exhibition matters to you, check access before traveling.

## Getting there and adding it to a journey

Roads connect Colonia with [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and other Uruguayan towns. Ferries cross the Río de la Plata from the Buenos Aires side; schedules, documents for crossing the border and baggage rules should be checked with the current operator and the official requirements of both countries.

Timing matters on a short visit: explore the center in the morning, then spend time along the water or in museums. Staying one night allows you to see the old streets in evening light after day-trip groups have left.

For a longer journey through Uruguay, combine Colonia with [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and other stops from the [Uruguay tour catalog](/uruguay/tour/). Colonia adds historical depth, while the capital offers a view of modern urban culture.

## Frequently asked questions about Colonia del Sacramento

### When was Colonia del Sacramento founded?

In 1680, when a Portuguese settlement was established on the Río de la Plata.

### Is the entire town a UNESCO World Heritage Site?

No. The designation covers the historic quarter with its distinctive layout and architecture.

### Can you explore Colonia in a day?

The main historic quarter can be explored on foot in one day. For museums, sunset and an unhurried walk, staying overnight is more convenient.

### How is Colonia different from Montevideo?

[Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) is known mainly for its Portuguese- and Spanish-era historic quarter, while [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) offers a much larger range of museums, markets and waterfront promenades.

## Colonia del Sacramento as an addition to an Argentina tour

[Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) stands on the Uruguayan shore of the Río de la Plata opposite Buenos Aires. Its historic quarter preserves cobbled lanes, old houses, small squares and architectural traces of Portuguese and Spanish rule. The town was founded by the Portuguese in 1680, and its historic quarter has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1995.

This journey is a convenient **optional way to spend a free day in Buenos Aires**. Ada Tours offers a standalone [“Colonia del Sacramento from Buenos Aires” excursion](/uruguay/colonia-del-sacramento/colonia-del-sacramento-from-buenos-aires/): ferry crossing, a walk in the town and return to the Argentine capital. It differs from multi-day itineraries where Colonia is already a compulsory stop.

Nevertheless, a town appearing in a tour's full geographical listing does not guarantee a dedicated walking tour of its streets. Some programs mention Colonia as the ferry crossing point for **another** optional destination: Montevideo.

## Which tours offer an optional Colonia visit?

On the [“Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazu” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/), free time in the capital may be used for several alternative outings. Colonia can be chosen as a standalone excursion alongside programs about gaucho culture and Buenos Aires' northern suburbs. The main itinerary remains focused on Argentina and Iguazu Falls.

On the [11-day “Argentina Deluxe” program](/multi-country/tour/luxury-argentina-buenos-aires-patagonia-iguazu-11-days-2026-2027/), a free day in Buenos Aires can likewise be replaced with a day trip by ferry to Colonia. The rest of the journey focuses on Patagonia, Ushuaia and Iguazu.

The [“Brazil, Argentina and Chile”](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile/) and [“Chile–Argentina–Brazil”](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-brazil/) itineraries are different. They mention an optional excursion from Buenos Aires to **Montevideo**, with a ferry crossing via Colonia. That crossing does not automatically guarantee a separate stop and guided tour in Colonia's historic center. This option must be agreed individually.

| Format | What the traveler experiences |
|---|---|
| Colonia as a separate day | Ferry and exploration of the town |
| Montevideo via Colonia | Another excursion, possibly with transit only |
| Colonia in the main tour | An already included stop |

If Colonia itself is your priority, explore [tours with a compulsory visit to Colonia](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/tour/). Its status is different there: part of the main route rather than an optional choice.

## What makes the day excursion special?

After crossing the Río de la Plata, visitors immediately notice low historic buildings and calm streets. The town is known for combining Portuguese and Spanish heritage; a leisurely stroll through the old quarter is more rewarding than racing to visit as many museums as possible. The waterfront opens onto views of the broad estuary.

The [standalone Ada Tours excursion](/uruguay/colonia-del-sacramento/colonia-del-sacramento-from-buenos-aires/) includes a transfer from the hotel to the Buquebus port, return ferry tickets and a walk around Colonia. Other sites on the route include parks, gardens, the coast and Real de San Carlos with its former bullring. Free time follows the sightseeing. Compare these arrangements with your selected tour's actual schedule, particularly if the free day is already occupied by another activity.

Colonia suits travelers who want a relaxed cultural day and a visit to another country without an additional flight. If you prefer a more intensive exploration of a capital city, consider [Montevideo from Buenos Aires](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/). These are different excursions with different purposes and sightseeing times.

## Ferry crossing and documents: what to plan

The journey begins in Argentina and enters Uruguay, so it involves an international border crossing. Before booking, check entry requirements for your **particular nationality**, the travel document used for the ferry ticket, permission to leave and re-enter Argentina, and the length of stay. Rules can change: use official requirements applicable to your dates rather than generic advice for all foreign travelers.

Allow sufficient time for the ferry and port formalities. Even if walking around the old town takes only part of the day, the full excursion includes getting to the port, the ferry, border controls and the return to your hotel. Avoid scheduling a late international flight from Buenos Aires the same day without checking the connection.

Conditions by the water may differ from central Buenos Aires. Comfortable shoes help on the cobbled streets, while an extra light layer of clothing is useful in the wind. The challenge of this day is usually travel time and the fixed ferry schedule rather than strenuous walking.

## Choosing between Colonia and other day trips

Colonia offers a historic town and a border crossing into Uruguay. Tigre and San Isidro, where offered by your chosen tour, provide a different outing through Buenos Aires' northern suburbs and the delta. A ranch excursion featuring gaucho traditions focuses on rural culture. It is not possible to fit all these alternatives into the same free day without restructuring the trip.


## Frequently asked questions about optional Colonia del Sacramento

### Is Colonia included in every tour listing Uruguay among its countries?

No. Several Argentina itineraries offer it as an optional excursion, while some routes mention it as part of the crossing on the way to Montevideo. For a compulsory visit, see the [main tours through Colonia](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/tour/).

### Can you visit Colonia from Buenos Aires without staying overnight?

Yes. The [Ada Tours day excursion](/uruguay/colonia-del-sacramento/colonia-del-sacramento-from-buenos-aires/) includes the return ferry and a journey back to Buenos Aires. Check your free day and the ferry schedule.

### Can you explore Montevideo after visiting Colonia?

The described day excursion focuses on Colonia. Montevideo is a separate product, and a full visit to both cities should not be promised without a specially arranged itinerary.

### Do you need a visa for this trip?

Requirements depend on nationality and other travel circumstances. Before adding Uruguay, check current entry and re-entry rules for Argentina for the actual documents and travel dates.
